newTerms.series one / two / three group: grupo de la serie uno / dos / tres

forcedChoices.reason: English 'must' here is an inference by the author; 'deber de' marks probability, not obligation.
Spanish 'equilibrio de poder' keeps both the sense of balance and of the deciding weight, as the English does.
Spanish 'sus' would be ambiguous between the Adjusters and the readers; the English 'your' is clear.
'master' here is the biblical 'serve two masters'; 'Maestro' is the glossary title of Jesus and must not appear.
Spanish 'compromiso' means a commitment (false friend); 'transigencia' carries the sense of a compromise.
Jesus speaks to the Father as one person; the packet rule gives 'tú'.

forcedChoices.choice: son anteriores ... son posteriores a la personalidad
forcedChoices.reason: Spanish forces ser/estar; 'anterior/posterior' keep both the sense of time and of order that 'before/after' has.
'order' as a class of beings is masculine in Spanish, as the earlier glossary forms use.
